subject: Chemistry
title: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry
summary: Oxidation is loss of electrons (oxidation number rises); reduction is gain of electrons (oxidation number falls). They always happen together — a redox reaction.
A galvanic cell turns a spontaneous redox reaction into electricity: oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode. Its emf E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode, and ΔG° = −nFE°cell.
The Nernst equation gives cell or electrode potential at any concentration; at equilibrium Ecell = 0, which links E° to the equilibrium constant.
Electrolytic cells use electricity to drive reactions (Faraday's laws). Conductance of solutions (κ, Λm) and Kohlrausch's law connect electrochemistry to ion mobility and degree of dissociation.

formulas.name: Oxidation number rules
formulas.formula: free element 0;  F −1;  O −2 (peroxide −1, OF₂ +2);  H +1 (metal hydride −1);  sum = charge of species
formulas.mistake: Peroxides (H₂O₂, Na₂O₂) have O at −1 — don't use −2 there.

formulas.name: Balancing redox (ion–electron method)
formulas.formula: split into half-reactions → balance atoms other than O, H → O with H₂O → H with H⁺ (OH⁻ in base) → charge with e⁻ → add

formulas.name: Standard cell emf
formulas.mistake: Use reduction potentials for both — don't flip signs and then subtract again.

formulas.name: Nernst equation
formulas.formula: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log Q  at 298 K
formulas.note: Q uses product/reactant concentrations; pure solids and liquids are left out.

formulas.name: E° and equilibrium constant
formulas.formula: log K = n E°cell / 0.0591;  ΔG° = −2.303 RT log K
formulas.when: How far a cell reaction goes.

formulas.name: Faraday's first law
formulas.formula: m = Z I t = (M/nF) × I t
formulas.note: 1 F = 96500 C = charge of 1 mol of electrons.

formulas.name: Faraday's second law
formulas.formula: m₁/m₂ = E₁/E₂ (equivalent masses) for the same charge

formulas.name: Conductivity and molar conductivity
formulas.formula: κ = 1/ρ = G × (l/A);  Λm = κ × 1000 / C  (κ in S cm⁻¹, C in mol L⁻¹, Λm in S cm² mol⁻¹)

formulas.name: Variation with concentration
formulas.formula: strong electrolyte: Λm = Λ°m − A√C;  weak electrolyte: Λm rises steeply on dilution

formulas.name: Kohlrausch's law
formulas.formula: Λ°m = ν₊λ°₊ + ν₋λ°₋;  Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl)
formulas.when: Limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolytes.

topics.title: Types of redox reactions
topics.explain: Combination, decomposition, displacement (metal and non-metal) and disproportionation, where one element is both oxidised and reduced: 3Cl₂ + 6OH⁻ → 5Cl⁻ + ClO₃⁻ + 3H₂O; 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂.

topics.title: Redox titrations
topics.explain: KMnO₄ in acid (MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺, 5e⁻) is a self-indicator; K₂Cr₂O₇ (Cr₂O₇²⁻ → 2Cr³⁺, 6e⁻) needs an indicator. n-factor = electrons exchanged per formula unit.

topics.title: Electrochemical series
topics.explain: Metals with more negative E° are stronger reducing agents and displace metals below them (Zn displaces Cu). F₂ is the strongest oxidising agent, Li the strongest reducing agent in water.

topics.title: Galvanic cell anatomy
topics.explain: Anode: oxidation, negative terminal. Cathode: reduction, positive terminal. The salt bridge (KCl/KNO₃ in agar) completes the circuit and keeps the solutions neutral. Electrons flow anode → cathode through the wire.

topics.title: Products of electrolysis
topics.explain: At the cathode the species with higher reduction potential is reduced; at the anode the one easiest to oxidise. Aqueous NaCl gives H₂ at the cathode and Cl₂ at the anode (overpotential). Molten NaCl gives Na and Cl₂. Inert (Pt) vs active (Cu) electrodes change the anode reaction.

topics.title: Batteries
topics.explain: Primary (not rechargeable): dry cell (Zn anode, MnO₂ cathode), mercury cell (constant 1.35 V). Secondary (rechargeable): lead storage battery (Pb anode, PbO₂ cathode, H₂SO₄), Ni–Cd. Fuel cells (H₂–O₂) convert fuel energy directly with high efficiency.

topics.title: Corrosion
topics.explain: Rusting is electrochemical: iron is oxidised at anodic spots, oxygen reduced at cathodic spots, forming Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. Prevent it by painting, galvanising (zinc coating — sacrificial protection) or connecting to a more active metal.

topics.title: Conductance basics
topics.explain: Metallic conduction is by electrons and falls with temperature; electrolytic conduction is by ions and rises with temperature. Cell constant = l/A, found using KCl of known conductivity.
